parts:
On Sunday, October 9, 2016 at 3:00:51 PM UTC-4, Bob Carpenter wrote:
I'm not sure what you're asking.  Was the error message unclear?
The argument must be declared in data or transformed data or be
an expression which only includes data and transformed data.

I think the parser is being a bit strict here. If the integrate_ode_{rk45,bdf}() function is called within a user-defined function, then it doesn't know whether the arguments are double or var arrays. Indeed, if the user-defined function is being exposed by expose_stan_functions(), then there may not even be a data block even though all the arguments will be double or int arrays.

Ben

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] fifth argument to integrate_ode_bdf (real data) must be data only and not reference parameters
parts:
I see. That's a problem for how things are defined
now in terms of constraints. The only things that constrain
source of variables right now are the integrate_ode expressions
(not ordinary functions).

All of the functions have been designed to operate on any
inputs, which is why a function that calls integrate_ode
can't be compiled---it can't guarantee that the argument it will
try to pass in will be data.

This is another one that's easy to fix if we let the C++
compiler blow up on the user, but I don't see offhand how to
fix it so that well-formed Stan programs always compile in C++.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re[2]: [stan-users] fifth argument to integrate_ode_bdf (real data) must be data only and not reference parameters
parts:
The problem is that the following is not allowed in the function
block:
functions {
real [] pbpk (real t, real [] y, real [] theta, real [] x_r, int []
x_i) {
real ydot[41];
return ydot;
}
real [] my_integrate_ode (real [] y0, real t0, real [] uts, real []
theta, int T, int N) {
real y_hat [T, N];
int x_i [0];
real x_r [0];

y_hat = integrate_ode_bdf (pbpk, y0, t0, uts, theta, x_r, x_i);
return yhat;
}
}

I don't understand why integrate_ode is special. I think I saw an
example where it is possible to call _rng within user function.

In this example it is easier for me to keep x_r empty (since stan model
is created by dMod) and presumably because of this compiler is upset
because real data is not provided.

Thank you,
Linas

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: Re[2]: [stan-users] fifth argument to integrate_ode_bdf (real data) must be data only and not reference parameters
parts:
Hi Linas,

integrate_ode() (and the other integrate_ode_*() functions) are special because they are. In this case, it comes down to how we've implemented the C++. There isn't a current workaround from RStan. I'm not sure when we'd be able to put one in. My guess is that we'll need a more coherent design between RStan's expose_stan_functions() and how the language gets translated to C++, but I'm always a bit conservative. Ben might have some other design in mind that makes it work without so much work.

Here's some more detail: in any of the other functions, any of the arguments that accept real arguments can either be (in C++) double or stan::math::var (the type for reverse-mode autodiff). For integrate_ode(), real[] x_r must be std::vector<double> and it must not be std::vector<stan::math::var>. When the Stan language gets translated to C++, data, transformed data, and generated quantities are always instantiated as doubles whereas parameters, transformed parameters, and local variables within those blocks and the model block are instantiated as stan::math::var.

+1 to what Bob's said. But, I'm afraid it might not even compile? I'm not sure. It gets tricky.

In short: integrate_ode() is special. There aren't any other functions that are restricted to arguments within certain blocks. Maybe that was a bad design choice, but at the time we wrote the integrator code, it was the only sensible design we could come up with that would preserve efficiency.


Daniel

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] fifth argument to integrate_ode_bdf (real data) must be data only and not reference parameters
parts:
> On Oct 10, 2016, at 5:34 PM, Daniel Lee <bea...@alum.mit.edu> wrote:
>
> Hi Linas,
>
> integrate_ode() (and the other integrate_ode_*() functions) are special because they are.

There are two reasons:

1. integrate_ode() takes the name of another function as an argument
which isn't supported for general-purpose Stan functions, and

2. integrate_ode() restricts its data argument to be data only, meaning
that it can only use values that are defined in data or transformed data
or only involve constants (but the latter case can't arise with an array,
so it really needs to be defined in the data or transformed data block).
> In this case, it comes down to how we've implemented the C++.

Specifically, it's a custom expression in the parser, not a general
function application.

But the real problem is that there's no way for Stan to figure out
in the context of a function that an argument to the function is
data only. That's because function arguments are allowed to be
any mix of data and parameters.

We could relax the constraint in the parser for integrate_ode()
and make it a run-time check that the values are not parameters
and instead issue a warning at compile time. That might be a good
idea here. I'll bring it up at our next meeting.

- Bob
